claims.statement: Completed response groups retain the last displayed final and fold preceding process records, including deduplicated observations. The final is excluded and a superseded answer can enter a continued response's process. Each response retains its exact loaded prompt. Complete responses can project a known zero count without an empty process disclosure; incomplete or unavailable responses remain unknown. Success accepts explicit final or legacy absent phase, failed/interrupted turns retain terminal status, and interleaved input, attachments and interactive items retain their source positions. Every completed native turn stays in the response ownership so independently observed activity from an otherwise silent turn contributes before a zero count is produced.
Response metadata presents compact duration and token counts with a deferred window-anchored hover overlay rather than expanded transcript content.
First-read conversation loading reserves a centered neutral surface rather than predicting the shape of unloaded messages.

Lazy shared popovers use the native material host when available. The GPUI fallback moves and fades the complete surface. Ordinary menu arrival keeps its resolved height and does not fade primitives separately. Centered previews use the shared interruptible height transition after their first presentation. Presentation entities request animation frames independently of keyboard focus while application policy permits animation.

The desktop delegates Mermaid syntax and layout to the pinned Ondine compiler, adapts its SVG for GPUI, and retains source fallback when compilation fails; integration fixtures cover 33 diagram families.

The transcript and composer use an 880-point conversation width and 16-point side insets. The composer overlays the bottom of the conversation, its measured height supplies scroll-content bottom padding, and the workbench editor caps editable height at six lines.
Voice history groups utterances by call occurrence, merges overlapping tails, hides normally ended empty calls, and anchors completed groups to their closing boundary across older pages.

Earlier native pages request at most 15 records and retry smaller dense pages; automatic prefetch waits for anchor restoration and can fill an underfilled viewport before requiring upward-scroll intent.

Model output, dictation and Live captions share grapheme-safe text reveal with immediate corrections and reduced-motion handling. Model output uses an adaptive 300–700 ms receive horizon and a bounded completion deadline; captions and dictation retain a 120 ms response horizon.

Saved edit recovery and history controls stay in Details. Active editing and unresolved-operation notices use the chat flow, while Fork progress and recovery for a disabled conversation use the feedback band above its composer. Failed input stays in the transcript and there is no permanent saved-draft list.
The task preferences panel exposes explicit native read and unread marks for the current root conversation, refreshes without acknowledging results, and discards observations when the source changes.

The Context defaults panel exposes native background compaction and marked client tool-output retention, shows effective and saved user values, writes native configuration, applies changes to new conversations, and refreshes after an unconfirmed save without automatically retrying.

Generated image attachments with a native fileId use the existing Stored description; fileId takes precedence over transitional inline result bytes, and the public attachment fields omit the file identity.
The generated-image media reader supports inline bytes, rejects native file references, and does not substitute a service-host savedPath for native media.
Current Mermaid integration tests preserve authored Unicode and multiline flowchart labels through Ondine; the retired local 40-cell parser does not define current syntax or layout.

Mermaid source copy retains original line endings and markup, incomplete or invalid diagrams stay literal, and the GPUI fixture verifies horizontal image scrolling without relayout in a narrow viewport.
Mermaid preparation disables image resources and interactive links, limits edges and SVG output, and checks the decoded canvas before SVG font parsing and image allocation.

Mermaid images are prepared in the background and cached by source and selected color scheme, bounded to 64 entries and 64 MiB. Retained geometry prevents an evicted image from shrinking a returning transcript row during restoration.
Local message delivery state is separate from the current editor; only positively unsent input offers retry, and retry preserves the original operation without replacing later input.

An unsent input remains an ordinary right-aligned, wrapped user message in the scrolling transcript. Its Not sent control offers explicit resend when permitted; the failure reason is a tooltip, and the message has no separate disclosure, copy or dismiss action.

The native transport observes monotonic intervals for model output, compaction, tool activity, automatic review and blocking user requests; it unions overlaps within each category while categories can overlap each other.
Completed observed timings are saved and retrieved for the exact Work, thread and turn; missing starts, unmatched boundaries, overflow and unavailable measurements remain unknown.
Visible model output is not full inference or a complete native critical path; the response details leave full inference, runtime overhead and other unobserved time unknown.
Clickable HTTP and HTTPS prose links preserve complete destinations and selection behavior; code spans and blocks stay literal, and explicit Markdown links retain their authored targets.
The Unicode math renderer supports structured display notation and inline zero while preserving original source for copy and for unsupported, oversized or nested spatial layouts.
Only rich streaming previews hold back unfinished Markdown link destinations; a completed link, committed newline or finalization retains source text, and code is excluded from holdback.
The call owner shows the voice waveform. Other conversations keep their editors and show a background call bar with owner navigation, mute and end controls.

Window and input-bar material preferences are independent; dark Liquid Glass shares surface opacity across themes while Thin retains its matte palette and the native input bar retains focused and unfocused glass styles.

Shared GPUI working/loading feedback and the welcome entrance use the Decodex cloud mark. SwiftUI account/profile/sign-in loading reuses AppAssets.statusBarIcon. Working text sweeps color without changing geometry, and reduced motion keeps the presentation static.

Cmd-F and the conversation search control find bounded loaded text including folded activity and retained live text. Only the current matching group opens temporarily, manual disclosures stay intact, and a retained current revision survives refresh and resize. Enter remains owned by Find; earlier history loads explicitly through the existing cursor and shortened output remains incomplete.
A collapsed command row shows only the native-retained output line count and removes its label on expansion; command text, discarded output and terminal wrapping are not included.

The composer prefers native dollars beside Context and can show an API-equivalent text-token estimate when native dollars are absent. Estimates show incomplete coverage and price age in the hover explanation; missing estimates remain unknown. Source-bound reads refresh after idle conversation updates.

Selectable text shows a hand pointer only over an admitted actionable link using current shaped text hit testing. Each paint recomputes the target, while ordinary text, empty space and unsupported destinations keep the text cursor. Existing click, drag selection and copy behavior is preserved.

Show in conversation locates an exact loaded item without a native query or displays a bounded native same-turn item window in the main transcript. The fixed return action restores the prior reading position, drafts remain intact, failed page reads retain the window, and item identities do not fabricate canonical timeline positions.

Completed-response and text-selection question actions open a native Side chat and stage a bounded, marked passage in its ordinary unsent draft. The source draft stays separate and selection callbacks reject a replaced source.

The conversation header groups a source and multiple open Side chats using confirmed native attachment identities. It scrolls to the selected tab. The + action prepares and opens an attached branch from the selected conversation's latest completed turn without a second confirmation or a message send, and reuses existing per-conversation drafts and navigation.

The workspace owns the attachment cache; a local parent link is only a lookup hint. Closing a Side chat hides its tab and returns to its exact source without deleting or archiving the branch; Side chats can reopen it.

An exact native provider mismatch shows the provider names above the composer. Fork creates and opens after source preparation without a second confirmation or Cancel control. Progress and recovery stay in that feedback band; creation sends no message and preserves the original draft.
Ordinary forks and Side chats pass the current reported native source model, reasoning effort and service tier; explicit provider-recovery forks use target provider defaults.
Project source tabs use Main, while Assistant source tabs use their conversation label. Side chat tabs use confirmed native conversation titles and numbered labels before a title is available.

Automatic conversation titles summarize the first completed user exchange, review after seven more completed user exchanges, and keep the current title unless the recent focus has clearly changed; generated titles are bounded to 36 characters.

Confirmed Assistant renewal keeps the unsent draft editable, loaded history and reading state. A saved draft follows only the same Assistant's recorded native lineage, including after restart; submitted commands and history references retain exact native identities. Context-spanning pages and cursors retain logical positions and exact native sources, while retired rows remain read-only.
Conversation layout uses a 20-point reading gap, a 6-point gap between a completed process header and its answer, and equal 20-point spacing above and below the 24-point working status row.
Activity islands keep a fixed drawable at the native window origin and animate a sibling foreground mask with the material contour, while mouse input is limited to the visible contour.
Streamed steps and their acknowledged native records keep the same process gap; final answers retain their streaming footprint until the completion transition owns process folding and answer spacing.

A native command exit code of -1 remains an unavailable result. Known outcomes use compact semantic check and cross symbols; unavailable outcomes use neutral operation icons and an explanatory tooltip.

The next-message suggestion uses the full editor width. Its distinct shared shortcut keycap and adjacent refresh control follow the final text line or wrap together without reserving a trailing column. The controls stay outside editable content and hide while typing. Clicking the keycap or pressing Tab creates an unsent, undoable draft. Clearing the draft restores the cached suggestion until a new turn or source change invalidates it. Explicit refresh makes one native sample request that asks for a different follow-up, keeps the previous preview during generation or failure, disables both controls while pending, and does not send a chat message. Generation inherits the source conversation's model and reasoning settings.

Composer and Menu Bar USD labels show two decimal places; positive values below one cent remain explicit as less than one cent, and exact zero remains distinct. The composer tooltip retains precise dollars.

The history rail highlights all measured exchanges intersecting the viewport above the composer, including multiple short exchanges or a long answer whose prompt is above the viewport. Highlights follow scrolling and viewport size rather than a single retained navigation target.

History previews use a 320-point width, at most two input lines and three reply lines left-aligned in one full-width text column. Input and replies use the same normal theme body color, font size, weight and line height. A shared 0.5-point menu-separator hairline sits within the existing 10-point gap without adding layout height and is absent when the reply is missing. Navigation excerpts retain up to 180 characters with an ellipsis when more text exists. There are no message-direction marks, message bubbles or speaker headings; short or missing content releases space.

The tick group and preview share one retained HoverIntent owner with 100 ms entry dwell, 220 ms departure grace, reentry cancellation and immediate explicit navigation. Scrubbing updates one preview without repeated dwell or arrival and preserves transcript geometry; focused checks cover text density, single-row metadata bounds, brief crossings and departures. History previews retain a 320-point width and align to the complete tick group's vertical center. First presentation resolves its final height. Later changes use the shared 200 ms Tween, preserve continuity on reversal and clip full-size text within the changing frame. Native and GPUI hosts keep the center except for the shared 8-point window-edge clearance. Reduced motion resolves directly.

Transient native popovers measure new content before placement. Ordinary menus immediately use the final measured height. An already visible centered preview uses the measured height as its transition target without an extra placement from a stale measurement.

Native response footers and previews share Metric symbols. Their caption typography and the sidebar time use ui_theme::metric_text and metric_ink: 10.5-point normal text, 14-point line height, tabular digits and muted ink at 85% opacity. Fixed vector input/output arrows do not depend on the font. ui_time owns relative ages and elapsed durations for conversation and Work views; durations omit unnecessary .0 seconds and use days with remaining hours from one day onward. Missing duration is an em dash and recorded zero is 0s. Preview metadata retains five equal-width centered columns for age, duration, steps, input and output. StepMetric keeps full wording and terminal status in its tooltip. Missing, zero, active and long values preserve neighboring allocation and prompt ownership. No call counter or second row is added. The final excerpt and metric row are separated by 8 points through ui_theme::METRIC_GROUP_GAP, with no second divider.

For qualified Codex revision 392ced7d3a9160fd35d40c606359869215f50522, mixed timeline boundaries use turn_id, started_at and duration_ms. Projection converts reported seconds to microseconds; saved-item history preserves startedAt and durationMs from native turn headers without resuming the thread.

Jump to latest message uses the shared MaterialSurface with Overlay material and glass-style preferences. Its 28-point control can expand to a 56-point working capsule. The shared opacity applies to the complete native composite. Click, Enter, Space and wheel-scroll actions retain their owners, and the attached surface hides after fading or when the Agent workspace is not showing the conversation.
